findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not migrated for new Clients scopes/resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns as soon as realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() exists. Realms initialized before this change only contain the Users scopes and the Users all-resource. After this change, the Clients scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite and the Clients all-resource are required, but init will never create them for existing realms. As a result, creating or evaluating client permissions in upgraded realms can fail due to missing scopes or missing all-clients resources.

findings.title: All-clients permissions are ignored when a client-specific authorization resource exists
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only falls back to the Clients all-resource when resourceStore.findByName for the specific client returns null. If a client-specific resource exists for any reason, such as a permission for another scope or a deny policy, the method evaluates only that specific resource and never evaluates permissions attached to the all-clients resource. Consequently, an all-clients permission such as MANAGE or VIEW can stop working for that client, producing unexpected authorization denials. The specific resource and the all-resource should be evaluated together.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal "Clients" type-resource name
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates over all resources whose type is Clients, which includes the schema's all-resource named "Clients". If an all-clients permission grants the requested scope, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that type resource and the method adds resource.getName(), i.e. "Clients", to the set of client IDs. This is not a valid client ID and does not represent all actual clients, so callers that use the returned set to filter or lookup clients will behave incorrectly.

findings.title: V2 has no cleanup for removed clients, and listener gating can be inconsistent
findings.body: registerListener now only performs permission cleanup when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled instead, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, and there is no replacement cleanup for client removal. Deleting a client that has V2 authorization resources or permissions therefore leaves orphan resources and stale permissions. If both V1 and V2 features can be enabled together, the listener will call the unsupported V2 method and may fail client removal.

findings.title: Client-specific denies can be bypassed by global canView()
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) returns true immediately if canView() is true. canView() evaluates only the global/all-clients VIEW permission or admin roles, not client-specific resources. Therefore, if an all-clients VIEW permission is granted and a client-specific negative VIEW permission exists, canView(client) still returns true without evaluating the client-specific deny. Explicit deny policies for a client can be bypassed.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only the Users resource type. For policies whose resource type is Clients, it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by client UUID and do not have a display name set, so representations or UI can show null or an unhelpful name instead of the client identifier or "All clients".

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when all-clients resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if the specific client resource is absent, AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource is called. That method can return null when the authorization schema is not supported for the current realm or resource server. The following call to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) does not check resource for null, which can cause a NullPointerException. hasPermission only guards against a null ResourceServer, not against a null type resource.
